messages.subject: Analyze 7.5 data orientation
messages.body_plain:
Hey Kylie

I noticed something odd, while I analyzed my data with Cardinal. The images have the wrong orientation. They are flip upside-down compared to the optical image and compared to ion images generated with Biomap or MSIReader for example.

My data comes from an AB Sciex 5800 and is in the Analyze 7.5 data format.

Attached are two images; an optical one and one from Cardinal.

Is there an “easy” fix for that or something I could do to flip them? If it would help I can provide you with some example data in the Analyze format.

Thank you very much for all the work and afford you put into Cardinal!

messages.subject: Re: Analyze 7.5 data orientation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sven,

You can do:

coord(object)$y <- max(coord(object)$y) - coord(object)$y + 1

where object is your dataset. This will reverse the y-coordinates in your dataset.

If you wish to simply flip the image itself when it's plotted, you could instead do:

image(object, mz=798, ylim=rev(range(coord(object)$y)))

which only flips the plotting y-axis and leaves the coordinates in the dataset unchanged.

-Kylie
